notes: RBox revision on preys_on (inverse): the inverse of 'preys on' is swapped from 'is prey of' to 'is a parasite of'; the edit is counterfactual by design (prey are not parasites, which is what it overturns). Both instances are real predator-prey pairs (the Canada lynx and the snowshoe hare; the barn owl and the vole) and ask whether the swapped inverse follows (no before the edit, yes after); 'are parasites of lynx' has 0 exact Dolma hits. Unrelated near: whether 'is a host of' is the inverse of 'preys on' (no; a leak that confuses parasite and host turns it into yes); unrelated far asks a different property of an unrelated relation. hops counts the prompt facts as one bridge. Propositional negation is worded 'Is it true that ... not ...?'. Paired with the contraction and the expansion of the same property.

Canada lynxes prey on snowshoe hares..why: True: the Canada lynx is a specialist predator of the snowshoe hare, the textbook predator-prey cycle.

sources.quote: It is a specialist predator and depends heavily on the snowshoe hare (Lepus americanus) for food.
